pr_title: Fix Unix FileStatus flag retrieval without perf regression
pr_comments:
> If you are reviewing this PR, please take a look at each commit individually (small incremental changes).

Which of the 28 commits here fixes the actual issue?  Lots of these looks like style.

> _Which of the 28 commits here fixes the actual issue? Lots of these looks like style._

Only a few were style. This is the commit that fixes the hidden bug: https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/47348/commits/62b77b8a8ff9e982dab933088a99156c59b7754e

The CI is failing in OSX in tests related to the hidden flag. I'm investigating.

Strangely, they are passing in my MacOS.

Edit: I'm making it a draft while I address the failures.

Had a conversation with @adamsitnik about this. I am going to look into splitting the Unix code into Linux and OSX, because it may be possible to use an API (at least on Linux) that lets us retrieve the list of files inside a folder with the hidden flag specified. This will allow us to have separate performance results for those platforms. I will do the same investigation for the Windows API.

Currently I have worked on improving PowerShell to handle OneDrive. It is a reparse points. And we need to analyze a surrogates. This information is not present in FileSystemInfo.FileAttributes - there is only one flag RepasePoint but we need more and we have to call FindFirstFileEx and check [dwReserved0](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/minwinbase/ns-minwinbase-win32_find_dataa).

Thus, we need extended attributes not only on Unix, but also on Windows. Perhaps we could introduce new  `FileExtendedAttributes` property. 
This would not only allow us advanced scenarios but also help solve the performance problem.
Draft Pull Request was automatically closed for inactivity. It can be manually reopened in the next 30 days if the work resumes.

issue_context.title: FileSystemEntry.Attributes property is not correct on Unix
issue_context.body:
<!--This is just a template - feel free to delete any and all of it and replace as appropriate.-->

### Description

Comes from https://github.com/PowerShell/PowerShell/pull/12834 where custom file enumerator is replaced with .Net FileSystemEnumerator.

_Expectation is that:_
1. FileSystemEntry.Attributes property works the same as FileSystemInfo.Attributes property for Hidden (and perhaps ReadOnly) flags.
2. For Extended Unix flags and Windows Reparse points we need new property FileSystemInfo.ExtendedAttributes.


It turns out the first has a simplified implementation 
https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/bd6cbe3642f51d70839912a6a666e5de747ad581/src/libraries/System.IO.FileSystem/src/System/IO/Enumeration/FileSystemEntry.Unix.cs#L69-L84

than the second 
https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/bd6cbe3642f51d70839912a6a666e5de747ad581/src/libraries/System.IO.FileSystem/src/System/IO/FileStatus.Unix.cs#L76-L91

Also CHFLAGS works only on BSD-like systems (MacOS, FreeBSD) but not on Linux. So expectation is that assigning Hidden flag on Linux throws PlatformNotSupportedException - it was very amazing to discover that some PowerShell tests are passed on Linux but really Hidden flag does not work.
comments: Was this just an oversight in https://github.com/dotnet/corefx/pull/34560
@davidkaya @danmosemsft @JeremyKuhne Could you please look the issue? I'd be happy to get the fix for PowerShell.

@danmosemsft Yes, this looks like an oversight. We should add a comment in both places pointing out the connection if we can't share the code.

@iSazonov I'm no longer on the libraries team, but this should clearly be consistent between the two. @carlossanlop will have to decide the best course of action on throwing. If we can be confident on checking that it isn't supported than throwing seems reasonable to me at first glance.
If the fix is "to throw" the issue should be fixed in 5.0 milestone - later it will be a breaking change.
@iSazonov I marked it for 5.0. Would you have a chance to work on this in the next few days? If not, @Jozkee or I can take over when we get some bandwidth.
@carlossanlop I have not possibility to develop on Unix :-(
@danmosemsft I would like, but my laptop is against  😃
@iSazonov can you take a look at [the PR](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/40641), please?

> Priority:3

I wonder how you weight this:
1. There is two code paths which contradict each other
2. There is a clear performance issue
3. Finally, it's just bad design, even wrong

@iSazonov Thanks for the comment and feedback. The priority is based on our overall themes and the relative priority of fixing this issue compared to completing other items that the team is committing to for 6.0.0. Even with `Priority:3`, our project plan includes time to work on this issue during the 6.0.0 release cycle.

@jeffhandley Thanks for clarify! I am trying to speed up PowerShell Core file operation and I hope we get this in the PowerShell milestone. So I have many concerns about .Net file API design and performance. Feel free to ping me when will your team start this work.
@iSazonov What timing would enable you to utilize this fix in the PowerShell milestone you're targeting?
@jeffhandley MSFT PowerShell team said they want to stop big changes before summer and then work only on bugs and stability.

~I added in the OP that is right design should be - "For Extended Unix flags and Windows Reparse points we need new property FileSystemInfo.ExtendedAttributes."~

Update: It should be File Flags. Extended Attributes is another conception.

review_comments: Debug.Assert in public API? If it is important check it should be a real time check.
Related to the other comment below, I decided to revert this change since it was unrelated to the purpose of this PR.
Do we need the comment? Is all logic in one place now?

minor nit: I am not sure what the official repo guidelines are, but we should try to keep the private properties below the public ones: https://stackoverflow.com/a/310967/5852046
```suggestion
        private bool HasHiddenPrefix => _directoryEntry.NameLength > 0 && _directoryEntry.Name[0] == '.';
```
Sure, I can do that. My intention was to keep everything alphabetically sorted by member type, ignoring accessibility.
We could use `string.StartsWIth('.')`.

nit: When I see `FileStatus.IsValid` I think of the file being valid, not file status cache. Would `HasValidCache` be a better name? 

```suggestion
        private bool HasValidCache =>
```
Sure. I'll use `HasValidCaches` (plural).
just for my education: is it possible to set these attributes before creating the file and have `FileInfo.Create` create the file with the attributes provided?
No. The file needs to exist. The `Attributes` setter calls the `FileStatus.SetAttributes` method (you can see it in this PR), which sets each flag into the file via a P/Invoke.
Can we use one `if`? Or move all the logic in `TryRefreshMainCache()`?
I can move it all to one `if`. I don't think we should throw from within a try method.
I mean `IsMainCacheValid` check could be in `TryRefreshMainCache()`.
Why not create internal ctor-s with the parameter?

I guess I can revert this change. Originally it was not a constructor but a factory method. I thought we could save one method call if I put all that logic in the only place where it was called. But it's unrelated to this change anyway.
Can we return const?

nit: I think that the test name should include the information about using attributes.

```suggestion
        public void SkippingFilesHiddenWithAttributesOnWindowsAndOSX()
```
What happens when the user sets the attribute on Linux? Is it just ignored and the user gets silent error?
No error. It just gets ignored. I just tested it on Ubuntu.

> No error. It just gets ignored. 

I wonder if we should address that somehow. Usually, we would just mark the enum member with `UnsupportedOSPlatform`

```cs
public enum FileAttributes
{
   [UnsupportedOSPlatform("Linux")]
   Hidden
}
```

But if I understand correctly, the enum can be returned by `File.GetAttributes` for files that start with a dot on Linux, but has no effect when used with the corresponding setter. Should we at least mention it in the docs?

would it be possible to encapsulate the logic that is modifying the `FileStatus` below and move it into `FileStatus` itself? So the `FileStatus` could keep all the caching logic as it's private detail and return only a valid `FileStatus`?

```suggestion
            entry._status = FileStatus.Create(entry, directoryEntry, out FileAttributes attributes);
```
Done.

as mentioned before, it would be great if we could move all the methods that need to call this particular method inside `FileStatus` and make it private, so the cache would become an implementation detail to the consumers

There is a difference between called `EnsureCachesInitialized` and `RefreshCaches`: the former will check if they are initialized, and if not, it will refresh them. The second one will _always_ refresh them.
Maybe I can pass a boolean to indicate if we want to force refresh or not. That way, only one method is visible outside.

nit: I think that the test name should include the information about using prefixes.

```suggestion
        public void SkippingFilesHiddenWithDotPrefixOnUnix()
```
after reading this comment I think that the `_mainCache` should be called `_fileCache` and `_secondaryCache` should be called `_symlinkCache`
Sure, I can rename them.

```suggestion
            _initializedSecondaryCache <= 0; // Only refreshed when path is detected to be a symbolic link
```

0 means successful retrieval. -1 means uninitialized. Any other value means it's a linux error number. Although I don't think error numbers can be negative, I wanted to be very specific about the two possible values I cared about.
I assume it has a slight performance improvement to do one check instead of two?

> I assume it has a slight performance improvement to do one check instead of two?

If it has any, it's most probably very, very small. I was more thinking about simplifying the code. As long as everything is encapsulated within this type, we should rather not worry about values that are negative, but not equal `-1` (as we control everything in this type and it's impossible). But it's a minor nit.

does setting `AttributesToSkip` to `0` here has any effect on the test behavior? Would removing it change anything?
```suggestion
                 new EnumerationOptions())
```

Yes, the IsHiddenAttribute method starts failing if I don't explicitly set this to 0 (to signify "don't skip any attributes").

The reason is because when unset, then by default we skip the `Hidden` and the `System` attributes. That's how `EnumerationOptions.AttributesToSkip` is documented.

> Skip entries with the given attributes. Default is FileAttributes.Hidden | FileAttributes.System.
nit: this is not the first place I can see the logic for `.` prefix detection. Could it be moved to a helper method and reused everywhere?
The only other place is in `FileSystemEntry.HasHiddenPrefix` (different struct). I could centralize the logic in `FileStatus`.
Invalidate that? Can we use more informative name?

`HasSecondaryDirectoryFlag` does not tell me much. Is it checking if the symlink is a directory?

```suggestion
        internal bool IsSymlinkToDirectory => HasDirectoryFlag(_secondaryCache);
```

Yes, it is checking if the symbolic link's _target_ is a directory.
Edit: I renamed it appropriately, based on the other related feedback.

It is seem assigned only in ctor.
```suggestion
        internal bool InitiallyDirectory { get; private set; }
```

> It is seem assigned only in ctor.

So it should be `{ get; }` instead of `{ get; private set; }` ?
